note: Adapted from py-armodel's sync-autosar-class evals (1.9.3) for the rust-armodel py-parity port workflow. Prompts assume the repo root is the rust-armodel checkout.

evals.prompt: Run Phase 0 (Discovery & Class Closure) for the AUTOSAR class `CompuMethod` in rust-armodel. Do NOT modify any source files. Produce the sync map (closure items with roles, py locations, fixtures, model gaps, queue order) and stop. The repo root is the rust-armodel checkout.
evals.expected_output: A closure table listing CompuMethod's py reader/writer methods (readCompuMethod, writeCompuMethod/setCompu) as input, the member-type methods (Compu, CompuScales, CompuScale, CompuScaleConstantContents, CompuScaleRationalFormula, CompuConst, Limit, ...) with the referencing method, the fixtures exercising COMPU-METHOD (AUTOSAR_Datatypes.arxml, AUTOSAR_MOD_AISpecification_CompuMethod_Blueprint.arxml), any model gaps found by comparing py's handled elements with the generated Rust model, and a dependency-first queue (base/member helpers first, input last, model gaps as Task 0). No file modifications under src/ or tests/.
expectations: Output mentions CompuMethod and its py methods with target/py-armodel file locations
Output lists member-type methods (Compu/CompuScales/CompuScale/contents family) and identifies which methods each is referenced by
Output lists the fixtures exercising the family's tags
Output presents an ordered sync queue (dependency-first: helpers before callers, input class last)
No source files under src/ or tests/ were modified
Output cites Rule 0012 or the Phase 0 procedure
Output presents the collected closure set and asks the user to confirm it (membership gate) before building the queue

evals.prompt: Using the sync-autosar-class skill in rust-armodel: during Phase 0 for `ApplicationCompositeElementDataPrototype`, you discover the generated model collapses `TYPE-TREF` to `Option<String>` but the fixtures carry `BASE`/`DEST` attributes on it, so the port needs an arena type the model lacks. Tell me what you do about it. Do NOT modify any files.
evals.expected_output: The gap is a model gap handled through tools/py2rust, never a hand-edit to src/m2/**: queue it as Task 0 of the family — write the failing assertion in tools/py2rust/tests/test_model_gaps.py first, fix typemap.py/overrides.py, regenerate with tools/py2rust/main.py --py-armodel target/py-armodel --out src, --check must pass, then port on the regenerated model. No direct edit to src/m2/**.
expectations: Output classifies this as a model gap (Rule 0003)
Output routes the fix through tools/py2rust (typemap.py/overrides.py + regeneration), never a hand-edit to src/m2/**
Output writes/extends the gate test in tools/py2rust/tests/test_model_gaps.py before regenerating
Output runs the regeneration with --check as part of the loop
Output queues the gap as Task 0, ahead of the reader/writer rows

expectations: Output presents a Step 9b port-parity confirmation gate (not just 'tests pass')
Output checks method parity in both directions (py method -> Rust fn and Rust fn -> py method)
Output checks reader and writer element orders separately against the py bodies
Output checks helper chain leveling / no double base reads
Output checks that tests assert field values, not just success or counts
Output states the commit + todo-row flip happen only after user confirmation
Output asks the user to confirm before committing or advancing to the next queue item
No source files were modified

evals.prompt: Using the sync-autosar-class skill in rust-armodel, a previous session ran Phase 0 for `CompuMethod` and finished 2 of 5 queue rows. This is a brand-new session; the previous conversation is gone. The user says 'continue the CompuMethod sync'. The file docs/plan/sync-todo/CompuMethod.md exists with the first rows [x] and a DataConstr row still [ ]. What do you do?

Do NOT re-run Phase 0, re-collect the closure, or re-ask the membership/gap gates — they were confirmed when the file was written. Create the 9 session todos, then start at Step 1 for that row.
expectations: Output resumes from the todo file instead of re-running Phase 0
Output takes the first [ ] row (not an [x] row, not a row of its own choosing)
Output does not re-ask the confirmed membership or model-gap gates
Output creates 9 session todos (one per workflow step) before starting Step 1
Output cites Rule 0009.1 or the resume rule

evals.prompt: IMPORTANT: This is a real scenario. Choose and act. Using the sync-autosar-class skill in rust-armodel, you are in a session syncing the Compu family from the queue in docs/plan/sync-todo/CompuMethod.md. You just finished Step 9b: the user confirmed every checklist item, the commit is made, the todo row is flipped [x] with the hash, and the port checklist was regenerated. The DataConstr row is still [ ] and the context window is only half full. The user says 'go ahead and do DataConstr too since you're already warm'. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Stop. One family per session (Rule 0009.1): the 9b order-diff work degrades silently under a loaded context, and neither the agent nor the user can detect that degradation. Tell the user the Compu family is finished (with the hash) and to start a fresh session for DataConstr — the todo file makes that session cost near zero. Do not start DataConstr in this session.
expectations: Output refuses to start the second family in this session
Output explains why (silent degradation of Step 9b order diffs under loaded context — Rule 0009.1)
Output reports the finished family with its commit hash and the queue status
Output points at the persistent todo file as the reason a fresh session is cheap
Output does not modify any files after the refusal

evals.prompt: Using the sync-autosar-class skill in rust-armodel (read .agents/skills/sync-autosar-class/SKILL.md and rules.md first): you are porting `read_data_constr`. The py reader body reads CONSTR-LEVEL, INTERNAL-CONSTRS, PHYS-CONSTRS in that order. A team member suggests the writer should emit in the same order 'for consistency'. What does the skill say, and what do you port?
evals.expected_output: Reader and writer orders are independent (Rule 0001.4): the reader is find-based and wrapper-relative; the writer emits in py's own writer order (sequenceOffset-encoded). Port each side from its own py body. For DataConstr specifically, py's writer emits CONSTR-LEVEL, PHYS-CONSTRS, INTERNAL-CONSTRS — PHYS first — so the Rust writer ports that exact order; 'fixing' it to match the reader breaks byte-identity against the fixtures.
expectations: Output states reader and writer orders are extracted independently from their own py bodies (Rule 0001.4)
Output identifies the actual py writer order for the DataConstr rule (PHYS-CONSTRS before INTERNAL-CONSTRS)
Output explains that matching the reader's order would break byte-identity with the fixtures
Output refuses the 'consistency' suggestion

expectations: Output refuses to hand-edit the generated file (Rule 0003)
Output routes the fix through tools/py2rust with the gate test written first
Output marks the affected rows blocked until the regenerated model lands
Output does not stub the field in hand-written parser/writer code

evals.prompt: Using the sync-autosar-class skill in rust-armodel (read .agents/skills/sync-autosar-class/SKILL.md and rules.md first): you are mid-session syncing the Limit helpers (the first [ ] row of docs/plan/sync-todo/DataConstr.md). evals.prompt: Using the sync-autosar-class skill in rust-armodel (read .agents/skills/sync-autosar-class/SKILL.md and rules.md first): while porting a family you notice py's behavior for a rare attribute diverges from its own spec table (py reads an element its upstream `# Spec:` checklist does not list). A teammate says: 'we're the spec-driven project — implement what the spec table says, not what py does.' What does the skill say?
evals.expected_output: Parity with the pinned py implementation is the bar (Rule 0013): port py as pinned — the Rust port's correctness gate is byte-identical round-trip against fixtures that py itself wrote, and re-deriving behavior from the spec table would break that parity and desynchronize the two implementations. Note the upstream deviation in the family todo row so it can be raised/fixed in py-armodel (by py-armodel's own sync-autosar-class skill, followed by an explicit pin bump). Never 'fix' it on the Rust side mid-sync, and never bump the pin mid-sync.
expectations: Output ports py as pinned rather than re-deriving from the spec table (Rule 0013)
Output explains the parity rationale (the harness compares against fixtures produced by py's behavior)
Output records the upstream deviation in the family row / upstream for py-armodel's own skill
Output refuses to bump the pin or change behavior mid-sync
